binning.rule: Reuse the six exact TASK-0010 edge arrays, fixed from pooled original Pythia response scores only; full [0,1] range. No new-data quantile refit, merging or smoothing.
binning.sparse_rule: Halt modelling validation if any measured modelling class/bin has fewer than 20 rows. Retain zero-count likelihood semantics in repeated controls. A repair requires a new version before reserved evaluation; never merge bins from final outcomes.

calibration.calibration_gate: No more than 1% unresolved LR-fit failures per cell and finite cutoffs; otherwise halt. Keep failures, no replacement draws. Freeze numerical cutoffs before independent validation and final evaluation.
calibration.cutoff_rule: Separately for each method/checkpoint/N, maximum of the minimum cutoff and the k-th LR over its declared f/alpha calibration cells. Source method maximizes over f only; simulation method over f and alpha. No optional cutoff selection after validation.
calibration.order_statistic: k = 1 + binom.ppf(1 - 0.05/144, 1000, 0.95), one-based. Use the kth sorted fixed-fraction LR including failed fits as +infinity. This is a conservative Monte Carlo tolerance bound, not a data uncertainty.
calibration.sampling: Independently redraw every finite class-template measurement and IID pseudo-data from the same specified empirical modelling laws, using actual audited template class sizes. Draw quark and generator components independently with Bernoulli probabilities f and alpha; share selected rows across checkpoints. Source stage uses Pythia only.

cohorts.algorithm: Existing exact-identity policy, lowest-row deduplication and conflict rejection. Exclude all 600k prior identities, prioritize retained new Pythia over new Herwig on overlap. Within generator, PCG64 class permutation in label order 0,1; first floor(n/2) template, remainder evaluation; sort each role by original row ID.
cohorts.evaluation_access: Integrity and label-count/role checks only until executable freeze and source/modelling validation gates pass. No score or label-conditioned feature performance inspection in TASK-0011.
cohorts.identity_scope: Exact constituent identities, not original collision identity; collision IDs unavailable. Labels used only for integrity, stratification, templates and pseudo-data construction.

freeze_order: TASK-0011 freezes statistical design, exact data roles, old bin edges, models/cuts, dependencies and audit code; no fresh scores
TASK-0012 freezes complete executable inference/scoring implementation after source/synthetic smoke, before any fresh score
TASK-0013 source validation precedes Herwig-template access; modelling calibration/validation precedes either final evaluation role
TASK-0014 scores the reserved final roles and executes the unchanged comparison
interpretation: Prospective reserved-event comparison after exploratory TASK-0010. Herwig supplies modelling templates; evaluation is within the declared generator family, not on an unseen generator or real detector data.

likelihood.auxiliary: Independent fixed-total multinomials for measured class templates, normalized separately; nuisance template probabilities profiled jointly
likelihood.generator_constraint: None; alpha is a bounded sensitivity coordinate, not a random-generator prior. One common alpha for both classes is a model assumption.
likelihood.original_cut: Reuse each original strict score > threshold and the existing unbounded inverse/delta interval, using efficiencies measured on the new Pythia template role. Never recalibrate cuts.
likelihood.pseudo_data: Multinomial at fixed N, positive class quark=1

numerics.normalization: B-1 softmax coordinates per class; no pseudocount in objective; logits bounded +/-35 with saturation flagged
numerics.optimizer: L-BFGS-B analytic gradients; initial alpha starts 0,0.5,1; independent SLSQP checks on declared source/synthetic cases and flagged solutions
numerics.scan_rule: Compare successive scans including unconditional/branch minima, preserve every detected component and bracket crossings. Stop at first stable component count/endpoints within tolerance; unresolved at 257 nodes is an interval failure. A lower profile minimum triggers unconditional refitting. Finite scans are not a theorem excluding every arbitrarily narrow island.

pairing_and_uncertainty.coverage_interval: Per-checkpoint Wilson 95% Monte Carlo interval and exact hits/attempts
pairing_and_uncertainty.event_pairing: Within each draw, share original class-row IDs across all six checkpoints and all estimators. Source and target populations are independent, not paired events. Keep seed metrics separate; no ensemble.
pairing_and_uncertainty.performance_comparison: 2000 paired bootstrap resamples of the 1000 pseudoexperiment indices per endpoint/f/N cell, shared across methods/checkpoints. Descriptive percentile intervals describe Monte Carlo precision conditional on observed pools, not an independent event-population bootstrap or retraining uncertainty.
pairing_and_uncertainty.scope: Finite pseudo-data and template statistics under the declared model; no training-selection, numerical-cut selection, unmodelled generator/tune, detector or real-data uncertainty.

primary_decision.failure_policy: All 1000 attempts form the coverage denominator; unresolved failures are noncoverage. Bias/RMSE/width use successful fits with explicit denominators and failure rates; no silent deletion or clipping.
primary_decision.improvement: Require all six checkpoints to meet coverage/usefulness/failure criteria and their paired descriptive 95% coverage-difference interval lower endpoints >0. This is a bounded consistency criterion, not a multiplicity-adjusted claim. If unmet, retain the outcome; do not promote a secondary contrast.
primary_decision.method_comparison: simulation_multinomial_profile minus original_cut_delta, separately for every checkpoint in the primary Herwig cell
primary_decision.secondary: Source-template comparator, every cell and seed, PID dependence, signed/absolute bias, RMSE, total set length/span and disconnected frequencies, boundary/out-of-range rates. No required bias or model win.

question: Do simulation-aware score-template intervals improve quark-fraction inference coverage over the original cut estimator while remaining useful, and how does this depend on PID?

resources.interpretation: 288k confidence sets include 36k source-only validation sets needed before Herwig-template access, in addition to the earlier pilot's 252k projection. Refined scans may raise cost; TASK-0012 must benchmark before launch. Checkpoint partial work at ceiling and review scope; never silently reduce repetitions or omit cells. No full campaign in TASK-0011.

rng.algorithm: NumPy PCG64; SeedSequence(root).spawn(cells) in checkpoint-independent cell order, with shared row draws across checkpoints
rng.cell_order: sample_size ascending, fraction ascending, alpha ascending where applicable; generator stages use independent roots

validation.conditional_evaluation: Actual class-template measurements fixed; IID pseudo-data sampled with replacement from the disjoint evaluation role. Report conditional coverage and finite-pool offsets separately from repeated-template validation.
validation.gate: For each checkpoint/f/N/declared variation, all-attempted coverage within five nominal binomial MCSE of 0.95, unresolved failures <=1%, finite well-defined sets and numerical scan checks passed. Diagnostic across the declared empirical grid, not simultaneous significance or universal coverage.
validation.independence: Calibration, validation and reserved-pool pseudo-data streams are distinct. No validation-driven retuning; fail, preserve and version before a repair.
validation.modelling_stage: After source gate, score only Herwig template rows and calibrate/validate the four-template model at alpha 0,0.5,1. Both final evaluation roles remain sealed.
validation.source_stage: Calibrate and validate source-only intervals on repeated-template Pythia common-law draws before Herwig template scoring. Include original cut intervals as a reference.
